answer: Registration demands a one-time memory-hard puzzle: each candidate derives a challenge from a fresh public beacon, burns real energy to solve it, and commits the proof to a shared atlas that rejects duplicates. Because the puzzle is memory-bound, one machine cannot cheaply mint parallel identities; each clone needs its own sustained electricity and silicon. Rewards vest in a time-locked vault, so a detected farm forfeits unvested copper instead of merely restarting. The cost is energy, hardware, and locked capital per identity, paid again for every clone.
